title: Contingency Hire: 14d Fast-Track Ops Canvas & Interview Rubric
content:
Summary:
This is a compact, operational playbook for emergency/contingency hiring and 14-day onboarding for critical infrastructure & SRE-focused roles. The goal is to get a new hire to production-readiness for first-oncall rotations and runbooks within two weeks while preserving signal quality in interviews and reducing risk from a fast timeline.

Who this is for:
- People Ops and Hiring Managers coordinating an emergency backfill
- Tech leads in infra/serving-runtime/SRE who will run interviews and early mentor shifts
- Solutions/prod teams needing predictable ramp expectations

Trigger conditions (when to use this canvas):
- Unplanned departure of oncall owner for production-critical GPU pools or routing services
- Severity > P1 coverage risk for >= 3 days without replacement
- Business commit requires capacity with < 30 days to deliver

High-level guardrails (must-haves):
- Role must be narrowly scoped to concrete deliverables for first 30 days (oncall, runbook ownership, a priority automation ticket)
- Hiring manager commits a mentor for first 14 days (min 4 hours/day overlap first 5 days)
- Interview panel must include at least one SRE/infra owner, one platform engineer, and a People Ops interviewer
- Candidate must pass incident-response practical and infra-automation practical (rubrics below)

Process timeline (target dates relative to offer acceptance):
- Day -7 to 0: Rapid sourcing + 1-pass screen -> schedule practicals; share short pre-boarding packet (hardware inventory, oncall expectations, minimal access list)
- Day 0 (start): First-day checklist completed (accounts + VPN + baseline readme). Mentor sync and role expectations.
- Day 1–3: Shadowing oncalls, ticket triage, read & update runbooks. Finish infra-automation sandbox task (practical).
- Day 4–7: Paired ownership for low-risk incidents, complete first non-customer-facing automation to reduce toil. Onboard to observability & tracing.
- Day 8–14: Gradual handoff to solo ownership for low to medium incidents; knowledge-transfer session with cross-team owners. First 7-day retro & ramp metrics review at day 14.

Interview rubric (fast-track & practical-first):
- Structure: 45m practical exercise (take-home or remote pair), 30m incident simulation, 30m culture/communication + 15m hiring manager wrap
- Scoring: 1–5 scale per axis; pass threshold = >= 3 on all axes AND average >= 3.6

Rubric axes (definitions + sample questions/practicals):
1) Incident Response (IR): ability to triage, hypothesize root cause, escalate appropriately, communicate under stress.
   - Practical: 20-minute simulated P1 (partial network outage to GPU pool). Candidate must outline triage steps, runbook edits, immediate mitigations, and postmortem notes.
   - Look for: calm sequencing, clear ownership, sensible rollback plan, and measurable mitigations.

2) System Design for Reliability: understanding of distributed subsystems, load shedding, failover, capacity planning.
   - Practical: quick whiteboard: design a fallback path when a regional serving cluster is overloaded; include caching and model variant routing.
   - Look for: explicit SLO/SLA tradeoffs, simple safe defaults, and fallbacks.

3) Infra Automation & Tooling: code-first approach to infra, idempotent scripts, testing, and CI checks.
   - Practical: small repo task—add a deployment healthcheck + a retry policy to an existing infra script (30–60m). Assess test coverage and rollout safety.
   - Look for: clean git hygiene, rollback plan, meaningful tests, and incremental rollout.

4) Debugging & Logs/Observability: ability to find signal in logs/traces/metrics.
   - Practical: given a sampling of logs and spans, identify probable root cause and a minimal dashboard to monitor recurrence.

5) Communication & Team Fit: clarity, collab instincts, documentation discipline.
   - Questions: Tell us about a time you led an oncall incident postmortem. How do you balance speed vs. correctness during mitigation?

Panel scoring matrix (fast summary):
- Each panelist submits scores on all axes. Hiring manager computes weighted average: IR 25%, Design 20%, Automation 25%, Observability 15%, Communication 15%.
- Decision guide: >= pass threshold -> invite to offer (contingent on references). Borderline (avg 3.0–3.6) -> short technical take-home + second SRE pair session. < 3.0 -> no-go.

Onboarding 14-day sprint checklist (practical-driven):
Preboarding (before Day 0):
- GitHub access requested and provisioned
- VPN/KMS access requested via infra-access ticket
- Pre-reads link: minimal infra topology, oncall runbooks, incident postmortems (last 6 months)
- Hardware & office logistics confirmed (if needed)

Day 0 (first 8 hours):
- Welcome + role expectations (30m)
- Security & compliance intro (KMS/HSM basics) (30m)
- Mentor pairing: schedule daily 1:1/overlap blocks for week 1
- Accounts smoke test: can run a safe read-only query and view traces

Days 1–3:
- Shadow current oncall shift (observe triage + pager flow)
- Complete infra sandbox task; mentor review
- Run through runbook editing flow; submit 1 small runbook improvement PR

Days 4–7:
- Paired ownership on low-risk incident or maintenance (mentor approves playbook changes)
- Instrument a simple dashboard/alert tweak and deploy behind a canary
- Security review of automation scripts with SRE/security buddy

Days 8–14:
- Solo ownership for a planned low-medium incident window (mentor on-call as backup)
- Deliver one automation that reduces shared-team toil (merge + release)
- 1:1 retro + ramp metric review at day 14; update development plan

Knowledge transfer & runbook inventory (must-do list):
- Inventory: list of service owners, runbooks, playbooks, escalation paths (must be updated day 1–3)
- Secrets & vault mapping: who owns which keys; rotate demo key for training
- Cost controls & reserved capacity owners: map out committed capacity for Dedicated pools

Mentor responsibilities (explicit commitment):
- Provide 4 hrs/day overlap first 5 days; minimum 2 hrs/day overlap days 6–10
- Triage buddy for first low-medium incident (explicit signoff before promoting to solo)
- Review code + runbook PRs within 24h (priority tag: onboarding)

Ramp success metrics (tracked at day 7 & 14):
- Can close low-risk incident independently (Y/N)
- Number of runbook edits authored (target >= 2)
- Automation merged and deployed (Y/N)
- Oncall pager noise attributable to new actions <= baseline + 10% (safety threshold)
- Mentor confidence rating (1–5) >= 4 at day 14

Decision thresholds & offer addenda:
- Offer should include a 90-day success plan with explicit milestones tied to the ramp metrics above.
- For contingency hires, include a 3-month review clause and a clear outline of expected oncall capabilities by day 30 and day 90.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: rushed access provisioning -> Mitigation: pre-provision sandbox tokens and limit initial scopes
- Risk: poor cultural fit due to fast timeline -> Mitigation: include explicit comms & async culture interview with hiring manager
- Risk: mentor bandwidth overload -> Mitigation: rotate mentoring load across two people, cap fast-track hires to max 1 per mentor concurrently

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm whether security team requires separate onboarding checklist for KMS/HSM for private deployments (ACTION: Aisha)
- Can infra team pre-create a ‘fast-track’ service account template? (ACTION: Marcus)
- Create a short Slack onboarding channel template that auto-invites mentor, hiring-mgr, and infra-owners (ACTION: Priya)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and tradeoff-driven. Looking for feedback on pass thresholds and mentor hour commitments.
- If approved, I will convert the practical exercises into a runnable remote lab and add to the hiring repo (linked_artifacts).

Quick links (references):
- confluence:OPS-FT-2025 (fast-track admin page)
- JIRA:OPS-4321 (automation template backlog)
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-scripts/pull/42 (starter sandbox task)

End of canvas.
